01

Priority

Character Maker

Mid-stage

The core editing path works for selected normal characters.

Available today

Normal male/female cards, asynchronous head 0/200/201 and converted asset selection, shape and color edits, static ABMX, and identity-preserving edited exports. Bounded decoded-rig reuse accelerates repeated normal-head selections while retaining actual byte verification. Maker-only bounded clothes groups reduce six GPU completions to four during the measured normal-head selection path. Reader-local verified RGBA digests remove repeated hashing within each head preparation without adding another pixel buffer.

Still to complete

Wider catalogs, special and modded assemblies, complete original editing workflows, and remaining owner-thread stalls. First selections still decode and verify input bytes.

Evidence & limitations

Clothes grouping measured 15–21 ms lower selection latency with about 5 MiB additional logical texture peak. The later digest comparison hashes 29 MiB fewer bytes per selection and measures 7–11 ms lower average API latency across four sex/cycle groups, with exact exports/resources. Owner-thread means rose slightly and individual stalls remain 61–113 ms. Each comparison has two process repetitions per arm/sex, correlated transitions and a background VM; no RSS or FPS claim.

Maker contract ↗Card preservation ↗Selection reuse evidence ↗Clothes-group measurements ↗Digest reuse measurements ↗Selection responsiveness #192 ↗

Base Models

Mid-stage

Six normal assemblies have bounded original-player comparisons.

Available today

Female and male heads 0/200/201 have independent neutral, repeat and one coupled-shape gates for both standard and bone-type-1 skeletons.

Still to complete

Only the original normal-male height coercion is allowed. The reference retains the earlier five corrected assemblies, exact identities, hashes and exclusions; CPU silhouettes establish geometry only.

04

Priority

Renderer

Mid-stage

Native toon rendering and an opt-in source-shader path are usable.

Available today

Metal rendering, explicit toon fallbacks, resource ownership and caching, and live translated source shaders in selected Studio scenes. The translated vertex path includes a host-validated correction for derivative quads crossing shared-vertex primitives. Selected original maps use baked lightmaps and compressed texture blocks.

Still to complete

Remaining material dispatch, original scene effects, resource limits, broader hardware validation and representative displayed-scene performance acceptance.

Evidence & limitations

The derivative correction restores exact repeated frames and own-triangle derivatives on the tested M2 Ultra/macOS host. It adds about 0.06 ms GPU time to the controlled 20 translated draws; default rendering is unaffected because the source-shader path remains opt-in. Map-specific costs and omissions have separate evidence.

Materials

Mid-stage

Selected native composites pass independent image gates.

Available today

The controlled ordinary female fixture reaches 20 of 20 live material slots. Exact stock cheek ID1 and face-owned lipline ID1 pass independent original target, cache reuse and transient-target release checks. Map 33 and 34 have selected baked-lightmap materials; map 34 also has a sky and particle-tree formula.

Still to complete

Other head/body identities, makeup and paint layers, patterns, states and whole-character shading remain open. Cheek/lipline comparative costs need a quiet run before the face path becomes default-on. Map realtime sun, shadows, light probes and remaining Standard terms are incomplete.

Evidence & limitations

20/20 is fixture-specific. Four lipline targets and two no-layer controls remain within one output byte. Fifteen recolours release transient targets. The seven-process app cohort improves the lipline fixture from 19 live slots/one fallback on the old store to 20/zero on the new store, preserving unrelated composites and control images. Default-OFF captures match; 78 Studio and 10 Maker lane checks pass. Unquiet lipline timings are retained as observations, not acceptance.

08

Priority

Plugins

Infancy

A useful bounded execution subset exists; general compatibility is early.

Available today

Translated profiles and three exact-revision native adapters: Mute, StudioAccessoryNames and HideAllUI. Selected mount, cancellation, failure isolation and save/restore workflows are exercised. Native save/reopen now retains queued destruction roots without replaying Awake. Rejected frames restore exact route history, including irregular time steps and lazy-clock ownership. Direct translated-profile/native loading and saved scene open, undo and redo reject incompatible candidate pairs before changing the live session. Disposing a temporary Studio model now releases its focus observers. Native library-backed scene open, undo and redo can now read attachments during read-only initialization using the candidate scene; the prepared session is reused after acceptance. Explicit initial library mounts also prepare attachment reads transactionally, with native save/reopen acceptance.

Still to complete

General DLL, Harmony, coroutine and Unity compatibility, original save adapters for arbitrary translated runtime state, and broader lifecycle coverage. Restoration still rejects initializer topology changes; detached preparation retains its attachment-read gate. Pending destruction combined with attachment-reading restoration remains an open reproduction task.

Evidence & limitations

Metadata inventory does not establish loadability. Direct mixed-graph rejection passed 13 Engine and 38 final Release app checks. Saved candidate restoration passes 16 focused Engine and 71 integrated app checks, preserving state and frames on rejection except the expected history error status. Original tampered-file errors retain precedence. Route-only checkpoint costs have a bounded quiet measurement; graph validation cost was not timed. Temporary-owner disposal passes 59 focused and 132 lifecycle app checks; the two retained focus tokens per disposed owner are released. This does not establish an RSS or timing improvement. Library-backed attachment restoration passes 9 focused Engine invocations and 105 save/reopen app checks, including cold candidates, warm-scene isolation, repeated read failures, exact rollback and cancellation. No timing or allocation improvement is claimed. Initial library attachment preparation subsequently passes 76 save and 20 fresh-process reopen checks, including cold/warm failure rollback, cancellation and exact fields/clocks. The earlier 81-check rejection diagnostic remains historical. Original scene plugin-data rewrites are documented separately from native translated execution.

How to read this page

Progress needs context.

This is a reviewed snapshot of accepted work, not a live test dashboard. Linked issues may advance after the review date. Detailed references retain their own measured commits, inputs and exclusions.

Mid-stage

A useful implementation exists, with meaningful gaps in coverage, integration, source semantics or verification.

Infancy

A scaffold or bounded executable subset exists; most original behavior or application integration is still missing.

Performance & fidelity

Responsiveness, total latency, memory and GPU work are assessed separately. Public CI cannot certify private original-player or GPU comparisons.

Ikkoku

Small, continuous updates. Traceable evidence.
